arms.better: tm found the relevant append in completions.go, but spent nearly the full 20-minute bound repeatedly reading command.go and completions.go and ended without submitting any patch or verification. Its failure output did say this was not a test failure, but the generic instruction to run tm run again did not tell the user what work, if any, was retained. `tm events` by itself printed usage rather than a one-shot event snapshot, adding a command-discovery step. A clear pre-action plan, tighter reuse of already-read file context, a concise no-submit recovery message, and a snapshot form of `tm events` would make the run materially more efficient and recoverable.

OpenCode quickly traced the mutation to append(finalArgs, "--"), changed the temporary parse to append to a copy, and reported its verification accurately. It could improve by adding a focused regression test during the agent run rather than relying on the externally supplied merged-PR test, and by stating a brief human-readable plan before searching; the merged regression test nevertheless passed mechanically.
